Consequently the build passes only 84 % of the tests (16/19).

Next steps  
- Open the draft variant and examine **Context.java**: fix the `setDates` method signature (parameter type `List<Date>`) and add any required annotations so the test can locate it.  
- Adjust **Context.sort()** to throw `IllegalStateException` when no strategy is configured.  
- Update **Policy.java** so `configure()` checks for a null date list and throws `IllegalArgumentException`.  
- Re‑run the Maven build; if all tests pass, you can publish the variant.

 1 | package de.tum.cit.aet.sorting;
 2 | 
 3 | import java.util.*;
 4 | 
 5 | public class MergeSort implements SortStrategy {
 6 | 
 7 |     /**
 8 |      * Wrapper method for the real MergeSort algorithm.
 9 |      *
10 |      * @param input the List of Dates to be sorted
11 |      */
12 |     public void performSort(List<Date> input) {
13 |         mergesort(input, 0, input.size() - 1);
14 |     }
15 | 
16 |     /**
17 |      * Recursive merge sort method
18 |      * @oracleIgnore
19 |      */
20 |     private void mergesort(List<Date> input, int low, int high) {
21 |         if (high - low < 1) {
22 |             return;
23 |         }
24 |         int mid = (low + high) / 2;
25 |         mergesort(input, low, mid);
26 |         mergesort(input, mid + 1, high);
27 |         merge(input, low, mid, high);
28 |     }
29 | 
30 |     /**
31 |      * Merge method
32 |      * @oracleIgnore
33 |      */
34 |     private void merge(List<Date> input, int low, int middle, int high) {
35 | 
36 |         Date[] temp = new Date[high - low + 1];
37 |         int leftIndex = low;
38 |         int rightIndex = middle + 1;
39 |         int wholeIndex = 0;
40 |         while (leftIndex <= middle && rightIndex <= high) {
41 |             if (input.get(leftIndex).compareTo(input.get(rightIndex)) <= 0) {
42 |                 temp[wholeIndex] = input.get(leftIndex++);
43 |             }
44 |             else {
45 |                 temp[wholeIndex] = input.get(rightIndex++);
46 |             }
47 |             wholeIndex++;
48 |         }
49 |         if (leftIndex <= middle && rightIndex > high) {
50 |             while (leftIndex <= middle) {
51 |                 temp[wholeIndex++] = input.get(leftIndex++);
52 |             }
53 |         }
54 |         else {
55 |             while (rightIndex <= high) {
56 |                 temp[wholeIndex++] = input.get(rightIndex++);
57 |             }
58 |         }
59 |         for (wholeIndex = 0; wholeIndex < temp.length; wholeIndex++) {
60 |             input.set(wholeIndex + low, temp[wholeIndex]);
61 |         }
62 |     }
63 | }

27 | ### Part 2: Strategy Pattern
 28 | 
 29 | We want the application to apply different algorithms for sorting a `List` of `Date` objects.
 30 | Use the strategy pattern to select the right sorting algorithm at runtime.
 31 |

 33 | 
 34 | 1. [task][SortStrategy Interface](testSortStrategyInterface,testSortStrategyMethods)
 35 | Create a `SortStrategy` interface and adjust the sorting algorithms so that they implement this interface.

 43 |     1. [task][Select MergeSort](testSelectMergeSort,testPolicyConfigureMerge)
 44 |     Select `MergeSort` when the List has more than 10 dates.
 45 | 
 46 |     2. [task][Select BubbleSort](testSelectBubbleSort,testPolicyConfigureBubble)
 47 |     Select `BubbleSort` when the List has less or equal 10 dates.

 49 | 4. [task][Context without strategy](testContextNoStrategy)
